title: Semi-supervised Domain Adaptation based on Dual-level Domain Mixing for Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: Semi-supervised DA: many labelled source images plus a few labelled and many unlabelled target images; region-level and sample-level source-target mixing give two teachers, a student is distilled from both, then target pseudo-label rounds (abstract only).
why_it_could_help_us: This is exactly our few-shot track setting (532 pool cells + a few labelled half-cut/new-layout cells + 1,152 unlabelled pool half-cells); region-level mixing would paste labelled half-cut regions (cut edge, scuffs) into full cells and vice versa, which plain 'add E1 cells to the training list' does not do.
risk_or_reason_against: Synthetic-to-real driving benchmark only; teacher pseudo-labels on 1-2 px cracks were weak in our SSL work (MT/pseudo-labels helped only at 5-10% labels); gain size not in abstract.

title: Semi-supervised Domain Adaptive Medical Image Segmentation Through Consistency Regularized Disentangled Contrastive Learning
what_it_is: SSDA for medical segmentation with a few labelled target images, using disentangled contrastive pre-training and consistency regularisation (abstract preview only).
why_it_could_help_us: Second SSDA reference in a grey-scale medical setting; template for 'pool + few labelled new-layout cells + unlabelled new-layout cells'.
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract preview only; organ-scale structures; contrastive pre-training already n.d. in our MIM/SparK runs.

title: Pixel-by-Pixel Cross-Domain Alignment for Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: Cross-domain few-shot setting for driving: training uses abundant synthetic source plus only a few real target images, with pixel-level alignment between domains (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Same classes, new domain, few labelled target images: closer to our few-shot track than episodic CD-FSS; gives baselines for 'how to use 5-40 labelled cells of a new layout'.
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract preview only; driving RGB; alignment losses on rare thin classes untested.

title: Anatomy of Domain Shift Impact on U-Net Layers in MRI Segmentation (SpotTUnet)
what_it_is: Supervised DA with 8 to 800 labelled target slices: learns per-layer whether to fine-tune or reuse the source U-Net layer (Gumbel-softmax policy with a regulariser). Full text: matches the best fixed fine-tuning scheme at every target budget; regularisation is significantly better under scarcity; encoder blocks (not only the first layers) are chosen most often; histogram matching (0.29 sDice) was worse than no adaptation (0.55).
why_it_could_help_us: Directly answers how to fine-tune C2 on a few labelled cells of a new layout: compare full fine-tune, encoder-only, decoder-only and the learned policy at 10/20/40 cells; the policy map also shows which HRNet stages carry the layout shift.
risk_or_reason_against: Gain is 'same as best fixed scheme', not above it; MRI scanner shift is low-level, our half-cut shift is partly geometric.

title: Robust fine-tuning of zero-shot models (WiSE-FT)
what_it_is: Interpolate the weights of the original and the fine-tuned model; on ImageNet shifts +4 to 6 pp under shift and +1.6 pp in-distribution, +2 to 23 pp on six further shifts (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: For the few-shot track: interpolate pool-only C2 and the pool+new-layout fine-tune so the new-layout gain is kept while CV5 (full cells) and the label-width convention of the pool are not lost (few-shot models learned the 1.5x wider E1 labels).
risk_or_reason_against: CLIP classification evidence; our two endpoints share an init so interpolation is valid, but no segmentation evidence in the abstract.

title: Surgical Fine-Tuning Improves Adaptation to Distribution Shifts
what_it_is: Fine-tuning only a subset of layers matches or beats full fine-tuning under shift; first-layer tuning is best for input-level shifts (TLDR).
why_it_could_help_us: Cheap arm for the few-shot track: fine-tune only the HRNet stem/stage 1, or only the decoder, on new-layout cells.

title: Partial Is Better Than All: Revisiting Fine-tuning Strategy for Few-shot Learning
what_it_is: Title and abstract preview: for few-shot classification, fine-tuning part of the network is argued to beat fine-tuning all of it (details not read).
why_it_could_help_us: Supports a partial fine-tune arm for new-layout cells; same idea as SpotTUnet.

title: Layer-wise model merging for unsupervised domain adaptation in segmentation tasks
what_it_is: Merges parameters of several trained models layer by layer to raise UDA segmentation robustness without ensemble inference cost (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Alternative to WiSE-FT for combining pool-only and new-layout models per layer (e.g. keep pool decoder, take adapted encoder stem).

title: Towards Fewer Annotations: Active Learning via Region Impurity and Prediction Uncertainty for Domain Adaptive Semantic Segmentation (RIPU)
what_it_is: Region-based active DA: score square regions by class impurity of the pseudo-label times mean entropy; label the top regions. Full text: GTA->Cityscapes with 2.2% labelled regions 69.6 mIoU vs 70.2 fully supervised; 5% regions 71.2 vs 71.9; thin class 'pole' still lags (43.8 vs 47.6 at 2.2%).
why_it_could_help_us: Gives a concrete protocol for labelling a new layout cheaply: label only regions where the C2 prediction mixes classes and is uncertain (cut edge, busbar ends, scuffs, crack ends) instead of whole cells; our few-shot track found half the cells gave about the same gain, so region-level selection may cut cost further.
risk_or_reason_against: Thin classes gain least; region impurity favours busbar/gridline boundaries (many classes) over isolated cracks, so a crack-weighted score is needed; needs an annotation loop.

title: D2ADA: Dynamic Density-Aware Active Domain Adaptation for Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: Active DA that queries target samples with high density in the target but low density in the source, with a schedule between domain exploration and uncertainty; <5% target labels reach full-supervision level on GTA/SYNTHIA->Cityscapes (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: The density criterion is the right one for a new manufacturer/layout: pick the new-layout cells least like the 532 pool cells (e.g. half-cut with scuff streaks) first, using C2 encoder features; no labels needed to rank.
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract only; image/region-level density in driving scenes; for us selection must also cover crack-free cells (false alarms).

title: Best Practices in Active Learning for Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: 3,000+ training runs over dataset redundancy, budget and SSL. Full text: diverse data favours single-sample uncertainty, redundant data favours batch/diversity (Coreset) because uncertainty picks near-duplicates (mode collapse); Coreset+SSL best on redundant pools, sometimes above 100% labels with <30% labelled; at very low budget AL is volatile and Random+SSL can win.
why_it_could_help_us: Our new-layout cells are highly redundant (same module, same layout), which explains 'half the cells gave about the same gain'; for the next layout, select a diversity-covering batch (Coreset on C2 features) of about 10-20 cells rather than uncertainty-ranked cells.
risk_or_reason_against: Driving and VOC data; metric mIoU, no thin class.

title: Realistic Evaluation of Deep Active Learning for Image Classification and Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: Journal extension of the study above: AL methods barely beat random once augmentation and SSL are used in classification; for segmentation, the best AL choice depends on redundancy, budget and SSL (abstract only).
why_it_could_help_us: Use as the protocol reference before investing in an AL loop: always compare against random-with-diversity at the same cell budget.

title: COLosSAL: A Benchmark for Cold-Start Active Learning for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
what_it_is: Benchmark of six cold-start AL strategies (choose the first labelled set with no labels) on five MSD tasks; cold start is unsolved but trends depend on budget (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: For a new manufacturer we have zero labels of that layout: the first 10-20 cells must be picked without a model trained on them; COLosSAL lists the candidate strategies (feature-diversity, self-supervised clustering) and their failure modes.
risk_or_reason_against: 3D organ data; abstract only; no clear winner.

title: Partial annotations in active learning for semantic segmentation
what_it_is: AL with partial annotations: annotate only uncertain regions plus low-uncertainty regions that are likely false positives/negatives; cuts annotation effort and training time without losing performance on civil-engineering damage segmentation (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Civil-engineering damage (crack-like) domain; for a new layout, ask annotators to correct only C2's crack predictions and high-uncertainty strips rather than draw full 24-class masks.
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract only; requires a loss that ignores unlabelled pixels (we already have ignore handling).

title: Hyperbolic Active Learning for Semantic Segmentation under Domain Shift
what_it_is: Pixel-level active learning under domain shift that uses the hyperbolic radius of embeddings as a data-scarcity cue (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Another active-DA scorer for selecting pixels/regions of a new layout to label.
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract preview only; hyperbolic head is an architecture change.

title: LabOR: Labeling Only if Required for Domain Adaptive Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: Active DA that labels only the target pixels judged necessary (title; abstract preview only); RIPU's table reports LabOR at 2.2% regions = 66.6 mIoU vs RIPU 69.6 on GTA->CS.
why_it_could_help_us: A cheap pixel-level labelling scheme for new-layout cells; we could score pixels by disagreement between our existing seeds (our idea, not the paper's claim).

title: Multi-Anchor Active Domain Adaptation for Semantic Segmentation (MADA)
what_it_is: Active DA guided by multiple anchors (title; abstract preview only); RIPU's table reports MADA at 5% = 64.9 mIoU vs RIPU 71.2.
why_it_could_help_us: Anchor-based selection of target samples; same family as D2ADA.
risk_or_reason_against: Weaker than RIPU at equal budget per RIPU's table.

title: MADAv2: Advanced Multi-Anchor Based Active Domain Adaptation Segmentation
what_it_is: Journal extension of MADA (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: As MADA.

title: Exploring Spatial Diversity for Region-based Active Learning
what_it_is: Region-based AL that adds spatial diversity to region selection (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Avoids selecting many adjacent regions of one scuff streak; relevant to region-level labelling of new layouts.

title: Adaptive Superpixel for Active Learning in Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: Superpixel-based AL framework for segmentation (abstract preview only).
why_it_could_help_us: Low fit: superpixels at 512 px will not follow 1-2 px cracks; listed to close the family.

title: Active Learning for Semantic Segmentation with Multi-class Label Query
what_it_is: Queries the set of classes present in a local region instead of exact masks (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Low fit for pixel-exact crack labels; could fit a cheap 'is there a crack in this tile' query for crack-free filtering.
risk_or_reason_against: Region class-set labels do not give crack geometry.

title: From Cold Start to Active Learning: Embedding-Based Scan Selection for Medical Image Segmentation
what_it_is: Uses foundation-model embeddings to select the initial scans for labelling, then switches to AL (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Cold-start selection of new-layout cells from C2 or DINO embeddings.

title: Integrating semi-supervised and active learning for semantic segmentation
what_it_is: Combines SSL and AL to cut pixel annotation in remote-sensing segmentation (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Pairs with Mittal et al.: AL+SSL on the unlabelled half-cells of a new layout.
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract preview only; SSL alone was n.d. for us at 100% labels.

title: Unifying Active Learning and Semi-Supervised Learning for Medical Image Segmentation
what_it_is: Joint AL+SSL for medical segmentation starting from ultra-low labelled regimes (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: As above, medical evidence.

title: Adapting medical vision foundation models for volumetric medical image segmentation via active learning and selective semi-supervised fine-tuning
what_it_is: Adapts a medical VFM to a new target with AL-selected labels plus selective semi-supervised fine-tuning (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Template for adapting a pretrained C2 to a new manufacturer with AL + SSL.

title: Selecting informative data for defect segmentation from imbalanced datasets via active learning
what_it_is: Title only (no abstract returned): AL for imbalanced industrial defect segmentation.
why_it_could_help_us: Industrial defects with heavy imbalance, like crack/inactive; worth reading if the AL arm is opened.

title: SelectSeg: Uncertainty-based selective training and prediction for accurate crack segmentation under limited data and noisy annotations
what_it_is: Deep-ensemble uncertainty filters noisy crack labels, SSL uses the unreliable part, selective prediction abstains on hard cases (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Ensemble uncertainty on new-layout cells doubles as an AL scorer; abstention flag for half-cut cells with scuffs.

title: Adapt Before Comparison: A New Perspective on Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation (ABCDFSS)
what_it_is: No source training: frozen ImageNet ResNet-50, small 1x1-BN-ReLU-1x1 adapters per bottleneck trained at test time on the few labelled support images with dense contrastive view consistency + prototype loss. Full text: 1-shot CD-FSS avg 60.7 mIoU vs 56.1 PATNet (Deepglobe 42.6, ISIC 45.7, X-ray 79.8); 5-shot 65.0 vs 62.0.
why_it_could_help_us: Transferable piece for a new layout: keep C2 frozen, train tiny per-stage adapters on 5-20 labelled new-layout cells with augmentation-consistency so they cannot overfit; cheaper and safer than full fine-tuning on few cells.
risk_or_reason_against: Binary foreground/background episodic task with prototype matching, not our 24-class head; gains shown on large-object classes; augmentations are shears (would need label-safe ones for 1 px cracks).

title: The Devil is in Low-Level Features for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation
what_it_is: Shows target-domain accuracy peaks in the first epochs because shallow layers absorb source-specific information and sharpen the loss landscape. Full text: fixing ResNet stages 1-2 at ImageNet weights beats training all stages (avg 57.21 vs 56.64 mIoU); LEM perturbs low-level features by random convolution with the Fourier phase kept; test-time LCM recalibrates with low-level query features; +3.71 / +5.34 mIoU 1/5-shot over SOTA (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Independent support for our PF finding (preserving pretrained encoder layers helps) and a concrete next step: freeze HRNet stem + stage 1 for the whole run, and add phase-preserving random-conv perturbation of stem features (keeps 1-2 px edges, which RandConv alone blurs).
risk_or_reason_against: Gains are on large-object CD-FSS benchmarks; the stage-freeze gain is small (+0.6 mIoU); our PF already freezes early.

title: Domain-Rectifying Adapter for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation (DR-Adapter)
what_it_is: Small adapter maps target features back to the source style; trained on source with local (per-image) and global channel-statistics perturbation and a cyclic alignment loss (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: The local/global channel-statistics perturbation is a training-time DG trick (like DSU) we can add to the HRNet stem; the adapter itself could rectify a new manufacturer's contrast before the frozen C2 decoder.
risk_or_reason_against: Episodic FSS framework; no thin-structure evidence; gain size not in abstract.

title: APSeg: Auto-Prompt Network for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: SAM-based CD-FSS with automatic prompt generation from support prototypes; +5.24 / +3.10 accuracy 1/5-shot over SOTA on four cross-domain sets without target fine-tuning (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Low fit: SAM-family features showed no crack signal in our probes; listed as the requested family member.
risk_or_reason_against: SAM ViT at 16 px patches is too coarse for 1-2 px cracks.

title: Lightweight Frequency Masker for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: Filtering frequency components of target features alone raised CD-FSS by up to 14% mIoU, explained by reduced inter-channel correlation; amplitude-phase masker (+0.01% params) adds >10% average (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Cheap inference-time probe on C2: mask feature amplitude bands per stage on held-out sources and see if crack recall on unseen modules moves; if yes, learn the masker on a few new-layout cells.
risk_or_reason_against: Evidence on large-object CD-FSS; high-frequency removal could delete crack signal.

title: Adapting In-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation to New Domains Without Source Domain Retraining (ISA)
what_it_is: Uses a structure Fisher score on the few labelled target samples to pick the domain-sensitive parts of a trained model, then trains only those, from fewer to more shots (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Principled way to choose which C2 blocks to adapt on new-layout cells (alternative to SpotTUnet).
risk_or_reason_against: FSS-specific evaluation; gain size not in abstract.

title: Cross-Domain Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation (PATNet)
what_it_is: Defines the CD-FSS benchmark (Deepglobe, ISIC, Chest X-ray, FSS-1000) and PATNet, which transforms features to a domain-agnostic space (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Benchmark reference only: its target sets include roads (Deepglobe) and grey-scale X-ray.
risk_or_reason_against: Episodic novel-class protocol, not our fixed-class setting.

title: Adapter Naturally Serves as Decoupler for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: Shows adapters inserted in a backbone separate domain information from content; uses this for CD-FSS (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Supports the adapter route for new-layout adaptation of a frozen C2.

title: TGCM: Cross-Domain Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation via One-Shot Target Guided CutMix
what_it_is: CutMix of one labelled target image into source images during training to bridge the domain gap (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Same idea as SSDA region mixing: paste labelled half-cut regions into pool cells during training.

title: A Novel Benchmark for Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation in the Era of Foundation Models
what_it_is: Compares VFMs under linear probing, PEFT and full fine-tuning for few-shot segmentation; self-supervised backbones beat segmentation-trained ones and the backbone matters more than the adaptation method (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Tells us not to expect PEFT tricks to rescue a weak feature extractor on new-layout cells; our A8 DINOv3 KILL fits this.

title: FAMNet: Frequency-aware Matching Network for Cross-domain Few-shot Medical Image Segmentation
what_it_is: Frequency-aware matching for few-shot medical segmentation across imaging modalities (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Low fit; organ-scale prototypes.

title: Few-shot unseen defect segmentation for polycrystalline silicon panels with an interpretable dual subspace attention variational learning framework (DS-AVL)
what_it_is: Few-shot segmentation of unseen defect types on polycrystalline silicon panels (optical surface images) with foreground/background prototype subspaces; public PSP benchmark; transfers to other materials without fine-tuning (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Closest PV paper in this family; its PSP benchmark could be a sanity check for few-shot defect methods, though it is not EL.
risk_or_reason_against: Surface optical images, not EL; novel-defect episodic setting.

title: Unseen-Material Few-Shot Defect Segmentation With Optimal Bilateral Feature Transport Network
what_it_is: Few-shot defect segmentation on unseen materials via optimal-transport feature matching (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Industrial evidence that new-material shift can be handled with a few labelled samples.

title: Two at Once: Enhancing Learning and Generalization Capacities via IBN-Net
what_it_is: Mixes instance and batch normalisation in shallow blocks: IN removes appearance (contrast, style) while BN keeps content; improves GTA5<->Cityscapes transfer without target data, no extra compute (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Our five sources differ mostly in contrast and gain; IN in the HRNet stem and stage 1 is a one-line architecture change that removes per-cell contrast, possibly helping recall on unseen-module cells of another manufacturer.
risk_or_reason_against: Needs IBN variant of HRNet (ResNet versions are standard); IN can wash out rare dark regions that define 'inactive'; per-panel BN changes failed here before.

title: Uncertainty Modeling for Out-of-Distribution Generalization (DSU)
what_it_is: Treats channel mean/std as Gaussian-distributed and resamples them during training; no extra parameters; improves classification, semantic segmentation and retrieval OOD (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Drop-in for HRNet stem/stage 1-2: simulates unseen-source contrast at feature level without touching 1-2 px label alignment (unlike geometric or blur aug). D30 proposed DSU via the IDA 2026 paper; this is the original.
risk_or_reason_against: Segmentation evidence is on driving scenes; may lower in-domain CV5 slightly.

title: Domain Generalization with Correlated Style Uncertainty
what_it_is: Extends style (feature-statistics) augmentation to model correlations between channels (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: DSU variant; try only if DSU helps.

title: RobustNet: Improving Domain Generalization in Urban-Scene Segmentation via Instance Selective Whitening
what_it_is: Instance selective whitening loss removes only the style-sensitive part of the feature covariance; robust to low light, rain and unseen structures, no inference cost (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Removes source-specific contrast in shallow features; single-channel EL has less 'style' than RGB, so expected gain is smaller (D30 judged it superseded).
risk_or_reason_against: RGB street-scene evidence; covariance of 1-channel low-level features may carry crack signal.

title: Semantic-Aware Domain Generalized Segmentation (SAN-SAW)
what_it_is: Semantic-aware normalisation aligns class centres across styles and semantic-aware whitening aligns their distributions, improving GTAV/SYNTHIA->CS/BDD/Mapillary (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Class-aware version of IBN/RobustNet; class centres for crack are dominated by 0.19% pixels, so it may help crack separability under contrast change.
risk_or_reason_against: Rare classes give noisy class centres; RGB evidence.

title: Style-Hallucinated Dual Consistency Learning for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation (SHADE)
what_it_is: Generates style-diversified samples from basis source styles (style hallucination module) with style and retrospection consistency; +5.05 / +8.35 average mIoU single/multi-source synthetic->real (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Our five sources give natural 'basis styles' to hallucinate between; feature-level, so label-safe for 1-2 px cracks.
risk_or_reason_against: Retrospection consistency needs an ImageNet model on RGB; synthetic-to-real gap is larger than ours.

title: Style-Hallucinated Dual Consistency Learning: A Unified Framework for Visual Domain Generalization
what_it_is: Journal extension of SHADE to classification and detection (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: As SHADE.

title: WildNet: Learning Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation from the Wild
what_it_is: Uses ImageNet 'wild' images to diversify content and style while learning DG segmentation (abstract preview; D30 judged it RGB-specific).
why_it_could_help_us: Low fit: needs natural-image styles; our analogue (external 11,938 unlabelled EL cells) was already n.d. as SSL data.

title: Collaborating Foundation Models for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation (CLOUDS)
what_it_is: CLIP backbone + diffusion model to diversify content + SAM to refine pseudo-predictions; +5.6% / +6.7% average mIoU synthetic->real and weather DG (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Low fit: three natural-image foundation models; none has shown crack signal on EL in our probes.

title: Textual Query-Driven Mask Transformer for Domain Generalized Segmentation (tqdm)
what_it_is: Abstract not returned by the tools; title indicates text-embedding queries in a mask transformer for DGSS.
why_it_could_help_us: Low fit: EL classes have no useful text semantics in CLIP-like models.
risk_or_reason_against: Not read; text priors irrelevant for EL.

title: Learning Frequency-Adapted Vision Foundation Model for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation (FADA)
what_it_is: Haar-wavelet low/high-frequency token branches on a frozen VFM: low-frequency keeps content, high-frequency branch learns and suppresses style; SOTA DGSS across VFMs (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Its premise (style lives in high frequencies) is the opposite of EL, where cracks are the high-frequency content; low fit.
risk_or_reason_against: Would suppress crack signal; VFM patch size.

title: FisherTune: Fisher-Guided Robust Tuning of Vision Foundation Models for Domain Generalized Segmentation
what_it_is: Domain-related Fisher information picks which pretrained parameters to update so generalisation is preserved; beats selective-parameter and adapter methods on DGSS (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Generalises PF (freeze-then-unfreeze) to a per-parameter choice; could be applied to the HRNet encoder with source-ID labels as 'domains'.
risk_or_reason_against: VFM evidence; per-parameter Fisher estimates are noisy with 478 cells.

title: Exploring Semantic Consistency and Style Diversity for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: DGSS method combining semantic consistency with style diversification (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Same family as SHADE.

title: Learning Content-Enhanced Mask Transformer for Domain Generalized Urban-Scene Segmentation
what_it_is: Content-enhanced mask transformer for urban-scene DG (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Low fit: mask-transformer decoders were not better here (no decoder effect).

title: HGFormer: Hierarchical Grouping Transformer for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: Hierarchical grouping of pixels into part/whole masks for DGSS (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Low fit: grouping favours blob-like segments over 1-2 px lines.

title: Domain-generalized token linking in vision foundation models for semantic segmentation
what_it_is: Token-linking PEFT for VFM-based DGSS (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Low fit (VFM route killed in A8).

title: Generalization by Adaptation: Diffusion-Based Domain Extension for Domain-Generalized Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: Uses a diffusion model to translate source images into many new domains for DG training (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Generative-style route; needs an EL-tuned diffusion model.

title: DGInStyle: Domain-Generalizable Semantic Segmentation with Image Diffusion Models and Stylized Semantic Control
what_it_is: Mask-conditioned latent diffusion with style swap generates training data for DGSS (D30 summary; abstract not returned here).
why_it_could_help_us: Already in MASTER; only after cheaper synthetic routes.

title: Stronger, Fewer, & Superior: Harnessing Vision Foundation Models for Domain Generalized Semantic Segmentation (Rein)
what_it_is: Learnable tokens refine each layer of a frozen VFM; beats full fine-tuning for DGSS (TLDR).
why_it_could_help_us: Already in MASTER; A8 DINOv3 encoder screen was KILL, so low fit unless run at high resolution.
risk_or_reason_against: Patch-14 tokens too coarse for 1-2 px cracks.

title: Causality-Inspired Single-Source Domain Generalization for Medical Image Segmentation (GIN + IPA)
family: medical SDG / random intensity + interventional mixing
what_it_is: Random shallow conv nets remap intensity (GIN) and two remapped views are blended by a smooth random spatial mask (IPA) to break spurious context-label shortcuts; designed for grey-scale CT/MRI (abstract; D30 read full text).
why_it_could_help_us: Still the most direct zero-shot fix for the confounders on half-cut cells (scuff streaks next to cracks) and contrast changes of a new manufacturer; 1-channel native; planned as gin_ipa but never run.
risk_or_reason_against: 3x3 kernels can blur 1-2 px cracks (use 1x1, cap blend); IPA must not be applied with geometric changes.

title: Devil is in Channels: Contrastive Single Domain Generalization for Medical Image Segmentation (C2SDG)
what_it_is: Contrastive training on shallow features of an image and its style-augmented copy separates style channels from structure channels; segmentation uses structure channels only; beats six SDG methods on fundus OC/OD (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Again points at shallow layers as the carrier of source style; a stem-level contrastive term between original and GIN/gamma-augmented EL cells is cheap.
risk_or_reason_against: Optic disc/cup are large blobs; gain size not in abstract.

title: Domain and Content Adaptive Convolution Based Multi-Source Domain Generalization for Medical Image Segmentation (DCAC)
what_it_is: Multi-source DG with convolutions adapted to the domain and to the image content (title; abstract preview only).
why_it_could_help_us: We train on five labelled sources (ARTS, CFVS, CSIR, BMRK, SDLE); a domain-code-conditioned head is a multi-source alternative to plain pooling.
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract preview only; a new manufacturer's domain code is out of range.

title: FedDG: Federated Domain Generalization on Medical Image Segmentation via Episodic Learning in Continuous Frequency Space
what_it_is: Multi-site DG via episodic learning in a continuous frequency space (title; abstract preview only).
why_it_could_help_us: Frequency-space mixing between our five labelled sources would be a multi-source version of FDA (already in MASTER).
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract preview only; federated part irrelevant.

title: Shape-Aware Meta-learning for Generalizing Prostate MRI Segmentation to Unseen Domains (SAML)
what_it_is: Shape-aware meta-learning across source sites for unseen-site prostate MRI (title; preview only).
why_it_could_help_us: Leave-one-source-out meta-training mirrors our unseen-module goal; organ-shape priors do not fit thin cracks.

title: Enhancing MR image segmentation with realistic adversarial data augmentation (AdvChain)
what_it_is: Realistic adversarial data augmentation for robust MR segmentation with limited labels (title; abstract preview only).
why_it_could_help_us: If its transformations include intensity inhomogeneity, that is the EL vignetting analogue (to check in full text).
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract preview only; deformations must be label-safe for 1 px cracks.

title: Improving out-of-domain generalization in Multiple Sclerosis detection and segmentation using Random Convolutions
what_it_is: Random convolutions improve out-of-domain MS lesion segmentation (small lesions) across scanners (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Small-lesion evidence for RandConv-type augmentation, relevant to small inactive regions.

title: Generalizing Deep Learning for Medical Image Segmentation to Unseen Domains via Deep Stacked Transformation (BigAug)
what_it_is: Stacks many image quality, appearance and spatial transformations during training for unseen-site generalisation (MASTER entry).
why_it_could_help_us: Already in MASTER; our house augmentation already covers most of it.

title: Position, Padding and Predictions: A Deeper Look at Position Information in CNNs
what_it_is: Zero padding makes CNNs encode absolute position; full text: boundary effects are largest near the border but also present at the centre; on Cityscapes DeepLabv3 with zero padding beats no/reflect padding, and thin objects near borders are hurt most.
why_it_could_help_us: Half-cut cells move busbars, cell edges and cut lines to positions never seen in the pool; a model that uses absolute position (via padding) will mis-handle them. Cheap tests: score C2 on pool cells shifted/cropped to half-cut geometry, and train with random translation/crops so position cannot be used.
risk_or_reason_against: Paper shows position information often helps; removing it may cost CV5; it is a diagnostic first.

title: How Much Position Information Do Convolutional Neural Networks Encode?
what_it_is: First evidence that common CNNs encode a surprising amount of absolute position (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Conference version of the IJCV paper; cite with it.

title: Convolutional neural networks rarely learn shape for semantic segmentation
what_it_is: Segmentation CNNs rarely use shape unless shape is the only cue; large receptive field relative to object size and a limited set of augmentations encourage shape learning, which helps on OOD data (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Crack vs scuff streak and crack vs gridline are shape decisions; if C2 uses local contrast instead, new layouts and scuffs break it. Their augmentations that force shape use are a cheap arm.
risk_or_reason_against: Which augmentations is not in the abstract; read before running.

title: Increasing the Robustness of Semantic Segmentation Models with Painting-by-Numbers
what_it_is: Title only (no abstract returned): a 'painting-by-numbers' training scheme to increase segmentation robustness.
why_it_could_help_us: Possible shape-bias augmentation lead; read before use.

title: Test-Time Training with Self-Supervision for Generalization under Distribution Shifts
what_it_is: Adds a self-supervised auxiliary task; at test time updates shared parameters on each unlabelled test sample before predicting; gains on classification shift benchmarks (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Per-module TTT on a new manufacturer's cells with an auxiliary EL task (e.g. denoising or busbar/gridline layout prediction); DeTTA (P459) is the segmentation version.
risk_or_reason_against: Classification evidence only; D31 found recalibration-type TTA cannot fix ranking failures.

title: Learning From Synthetic CT Images via Test-Time Training for Liver Tumor Segmentation
what_it_is: Test-time training for liver tumour segmentation learned from synthetic CT (title; abstract preview only).
why_it_could_help_us: Small-lesion TTT evidence.

title: TeST: Test-time Self-Training under Distribution Shift
what_it_is: Test-time self-training under distribution shift (title; abstract preview only).
why_it_could_help_us: Baseline for per-module self-training on new-layout cells.

why_it_could_help_us: Augmented-view consistency on the 1,152 unlabelled half-cells is the natural UDA arm for the half-cut layout.

title: UPL-SFDA: Uncertainty-Aware Pseudo Label Guided Source-Free Domain Adaptation for Medical Image Segmentation

why_it_could_help_us: We keep source data, so source-free is dominated by UDA (D31 judgement); low fit.

why_it_could_help_us: D31 judged organ-scale; low fit for thin rare cracks.

title: TTN: A Domain-Shift Aware Batch Normalization in Test-Time Adaptation

why_it_could_help_us: Our per-panel BN adaptation failed (false alarms); low fit.

title: Self-supervised domain adaptive approach for extrapolated crack segmentation with fine-tuned inpainting generative model
what_it_is: Fine-tunes Stable Diffusion with DreamBooth on the new site and inpaints cracks to create site-specific crack images and labels; training on them raises F1 by 25.82% and 17.83% on two target domains averaged over eight models, confirmed in a tunnel field test (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Gives labelled crack data for a layout we have no labels for: inpaint cracks into the 1,152 unlabelled pool half-cells (cut edge, scuffs) and train on them; targets recall on unseen layouts directly.
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract only; EL crack appearance (dark line with contrast halo) must be learned from 209 crack cells; a fake-looking crack teaches a shortcut; label width must match the pool convention.

risk_or_reason_against: Already in MASTER (BENCH_ONLY); class mapping needed.

title: Active Learning for Convolutional Neural Networks: A Core-Set Approach
what_it_is: Core-set selection: pick the batch of unlabelled samples that best covers the feature space (title and abstract preview); Mittal et al. (full text) found this batch-diversity rule best on redundant segmentation pools, especially with SSL.
why_it_could_help_us: The selection rule to use for the next layout: k-centre greedy on C2 encoder features over the unlabelled new-layout cells, label the chosen 10-20, compare with random at equal budget.
risk_or_reason_against: Classification paper; feature space must include crack-relevant features, not only global cell appearance.

title: Domain Generalization with MixStyle
what_it_is: Parameter-free module that mixes channel-wise feature statistics of instances during training to improve domain generalisation (abstract preview; IJCV extension found too).
why_it_could_help_us: Mixing statistics of cells from different sources (ARTS/CFVS/CSIR/BMRK/SDLE) in the HRNet stem simulates unseen-manufacturer contrast; same slot as DSU, label-safe.
risk_or_reason_against: Abstract preview only; mainly classification evidence.
